a.text: Let us continue where we left off. We tell of the lame scholar's disappointment and return, and henceforth, his melancholy of lost hope.
From whence does his story come?
Naturally, a painting.
What painting?

The scholar's loss of an old friend, his heart like unto ashes, and his decade of footing astray, before their minds once again moved in concert—he made his resolve, and devoted his mind in full, vowing to finish that lifetime's work.
To paint what?
To paint that never before seen.
How would he paint it?
He would think thoughts never before thought.

Ah, now that we're here, this has gotten quite interesting. As you all know, the limits of one's imagination are set at what one has seen, known, experienced. Relying on imagination to trick those, outlining that which is yet unknown, is simple enough. But to do so and trick yourself, that is hard as scaling the heavens.
After all, under our heavens, where can you find one capable of thinking something as yet unseen?
The scholar faced the blank paper and strained his mind for about ten days, losing more than thirty jin of weight. He had already been lame, and his appearance grew ever more fearful.
Come the deep winter, the scholar's house had long run out of food. His neighbors feared him, and none dared to approach him.
Until one day, the lame scholar again woke in a haze, his limbs powerless, yet his mind clear.
He knew well his limits were soon coming. He looked around him, his home a bare four walls and a dim room, and felt only that all around him was void, that he truly had become alone in the world.

The scholar gradually became unable to see the floor before him wet and frozen by the snowstorm, unable to hear the biting wind coming through his door and window. He opened his eyes and blinked, fallen into primal chaos, and felt that the walls were wandering far away, his desk dissipating, his brush, paper, ink and stone all ephemeral as smoke.

At a certain moment, he suddenly came to know the exact number of snowflakes in the flurry outside his window, came to know the angle of the moonlight and the truth of the clouds. He reached out fumbling for the curtain of night, and crashed to the floor in carelessness, but the floor was no longer a hindrance to his legs. He fell underground, and then flew into the empty depths.

He could not see with his open eyes, could not hear with his rapt attention, the darkness surrounding him whole—he suddenly went into an ecstasy, as if only in this boundary where naught existed to disturb him, he could seek his true work, rather than copy or desecrate that which already existed.

He continued to wait, wait until all had faded to null, until he could not feel even his own withered flesh, before he began to think—only when all creation and all beings had ceased to exist, and his consciousness was alone in clarity, had he briefly become master of his soul.
His imagination would never again be restricted, creating works of that which simultaneously existed and did not exist—on his territory of thought, all strangeness arose equal, and enveloped reality.

It was deep in the night, and as a teacher awoke next door, he saw the lame scholar's thatched cottage overflowing in brilliant light, spectral and dazzling, letting out all manner of sounds never before heard in life, defying description. The teacher summoned his courage, and stole a look through the wall.
With just that one glimpse, he dared not investigate further. He hurried himself back indoors, and for a very long time could not fall asleep.

The next day, neighbors thronged before the thatched cottage. They forced the door and entered, discovering the scholar's remains, and naught else inside. All thought he had died of cold, and as the village headman stepped forth to look, he saw sprawled before the scholar a blank scroll of paper, covered full in frost, and nothing drawn on it.

Afterwards, the people lamented that the scholar could not leave his past, dying obsessed in front of his scroll. Others said the scholar had long since contracted some strange disease, could not control his own Arts, and only thus did this strange case unfold.

The teacher, who alone had glimpsed the truth, never talked of the matter with anyone else. It was only in his final moments he told his son; that the disdained lame scholar, even his name forgotten, was a true master of all eternity.

steps.name: Villager
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Because that night, the lame scholar had in reality fulfilled his promise. He had, in reality, painted 'that which had never before been in this world.'

steps.name: Villager
steps.text: Why do I feel like the books told it pretty differently?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: The teacher had not the time to explain, or perhaps he simply swallowed the words he did not have.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Thus in the narrative heard on the streets, there is only the lame scholar's sails billowing with success, up to the fall of his senses.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: As for the truth of things, I fear not a single soul now knows.

steps.name: Villager
steps.text: See, though, what's so hard about drawing something you've never seen before? I could head back, smear up a scroll, and none of you would've ever seen that.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Ah, you can't put it like that. You've never seen a vast lake before, but you've seen the ponded waters after the rains. Let me tell you, lakes are ponded waters made vast. In the end, you've seen them before.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: If the lame scholar had strength, then this is where it lay.

steps.name: Villager
steps.text: Well if all that's true, then what in the world did he paint?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Who knows.

steps.name: Villager
steps.text: Look, could you give the contrived stories a rest? They're not exactly the most fun. Are you gonna tell any others?

steps.name: Child
steps.text: I want to hear the ending to the one with 'a lone soul ventures forth to Heaven, twin blade lovers that split the lands!'

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: I'll tell in due time, all of it. It is not possible to tell all under heaven in totality, and I use my scarce predestined hundred or so years of life to tell what I might. If I yet pursued thoroughness on top of it, that would be quite greedy.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: As you'd like to hear it, then next time, we'll tell of something else.

steps.name: Child
steps.text: Alright!

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: By custom, my mouth is worth no money. But when you've paid your tea, see what you might have for an old man's story.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: It seems we've got a few new faces today. Three mysterious visitors; I hope these strange tales of mine were to your satisfaction?

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Was that fiction?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: If someone told me a scholar caught Oripathy, and met his end in melancholy before his wishes were complete, then I'd certainly believe it was true.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Add some spice and flourish, and the story tastes all the better.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Quite sensible!

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: My thanks.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: However, I'm not sure myself how many really are true, out of all these anecdotal legends... I just have some interest in the field, nothing more.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: That said, while I might not be any kind of formal storyteller, I've spent a long time in the village doing it, though only the few you saw are actually willing to hear me spout my nonsense.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: I see three unfamiliar faces. What brings you here?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Ahem— (Gives a meaningful look)

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Ah—right, right, these two friends of mine came from far away, in search of someone.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: But neither of them are quite as aware of Yan as those of us born here, so I'm giving them some small assistance, acting as their guide. How should I address you, sir?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: It's been many years since I left home; I long since abandoned my old name to disuse. I fancied myself literary in younger years, calling myself the 'Umbrella-Boiling Hermit,' and though it's somewhat shameless of a title, I still use it to this day.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: How artistic! How artistic indeed! By damned luck, I too was given no option but to leave home, and nowadays go by 'No' and 'thing' in lieu of names sur and given. You can call me Brother No, how about that?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: (I told you that was a made-up name, didn't I—?!)

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: (Kroos? You catch something?)

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: (Eh? Uh, nothing, I just reckon it's really fun to watch how he lies himself a new layer every time.)

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: So we are both men fallen to the other side of the world. Then who's the person you three mysteries are searching for?

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Hah, just as the proverb goes, chance meetings are predestiny; it truly couldn't be more opportune if we tried. The one we're searching for is also a painter, like in the story we just heard.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: ...A painter? This village is modestly sized, and I've never heard of any painter here. What manner of man is this?

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Er... benefactor? May you describe?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: A woman. Uh, she should have big, weird horns on her head. And she can use some weird Arts. Also... also... she's a painter.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: And that's it?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: That's it.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: I admit, with that, I have even less of an idea.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Oh, this is a strange turn indeed... could it be that the one you benefactors seek left this place before we came?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: This village entertains very few guests. If it's as you all say, that strange person would have to have left an impression on us. I can get someone to help you ask around.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Good, good, then we'll leave you to it, sir, and for the time being—

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: We'll...?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Mr. Nothing?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Hey, what's up with you?

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Ah, heheh, where... where did we come in from?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: What are you talking about? Didn't we—

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: —Follow this pathway, and you can leave the landscape garden.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: Presumably you arrived following a crowd, and erred here? Haha, my garden isn't that big or small, but it's tough to find your way through it. Ask a servant for help.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Heh... Look at me, all befuddled. How is it I can't remember, now?

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: If you find any trace of that painter, and you need the help, don't hesitate to ask me.

steps.name: Storyteller
steps.text: I have some business for now, so, everyone, farewell.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Here, thank you, thank you, farewell now, farewell. Benefactors, shall we go?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Wait—

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: And that said, where should we take a look at? We've visited the teahouse, the stage station and the gardens. Where else could there be any clues?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: How long has it been since we got here?

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Oh, why do you ask? I'd say about... two or three days?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Are you sure?

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Ahahah, heh, most likely I slept awful last night. I'm a little out of kilter.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Lavaaa.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Nnng... I can sense it now... but it's so indistinct... it's like...

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Times like these, you've gotta go with your intuition.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: My intuition's telling me that right now, the situation's extremely messed up.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Is it some kind of mind-level Originium Arts...?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Nngh... if it's Arts...

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Benefactors, why the muttering? If we don't hurry up soon, it'll get dark on us.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: What are you talking about? It's still so light—

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: —The sky... the color?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Did we never look at the sky before...? We should've noticed any moment we lifted our heads... now that's odd.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: B... benefactors, what's going on? Look over there, is that... is that a moon, now?!

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: And it's broad daylight right now, isn't it? Why have they lit lanterns on the other end of the bridge?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Look behind you...

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Er?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: The horizon on the other side. Is that... is that the sun?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Hey. You think us coming back from there to here counted as 'going' one full day and night?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: This is really... new to me. Nian always told me that Yan was full of weird, unseen wonders... and landscapes like this too?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Uh, hold on, I think there's something in my pocket...

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Is this—the charm Nian gave me...?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Wait a minute... hold on! No, that's not right!

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: What the hell do I mean 'landscapes like this?' What was I just thinking?!

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Ah...

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Mr. Nothing!

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Er—? I'm here, I'm here!

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Is this Ni-weng Village or not!?

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Does... does it need to be said... er...

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: P—paying close attention, it seems a little off! But there isn't another village anywhere around!

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: This isn't right. It's not right.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Kroos, we left Rhodes Island, reached Kou-wu City first, stocked up, and then left the next morning.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: We were heading across the wastes for Mount Hui-ch'i, and we saw a crashed car—

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: —and then you two benefactors dealt with the beasts and saved me?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Just took 'em to a nice new pit to build their nest in, that's all.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: And then?

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: And then, we...?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Hmmmgh. Then we went straight up Mount Hui-ch'i, and found a thatched cottage.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: I pushed open its...

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: ...door?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Bells? Where are they coming from?

steps.name: Villager
steps.text: The bells are sounding? The bells are sounding! Hey, everyone call your families out! Move quickly!

steps.name: Villager
steps.text: What's happening!? It's been so long! Why is it happening today?!

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Excuse me! Can I ask what's happening?

steps.name: Villager
steps.text: Are you—are you outsiders? The bells mean monsters are coming from the west mountains!

steps.name: Villager
steps.text: Those monsters can't stand light! Just run to where the sun is and you'll be safe!

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: M—Monsters? What monsters?

steps.name: Villager
steps.text: Look, I've got no time to chat with you! Get out of my way, I need to bring my wife over here!

steps.name: Child
steps.text: Mama! Mama!

steps.name: Villager
steps.text: Is everyone here? We're still missing someone! Start looking, fast!

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Benefactors, benefactors, let us hurry and take shelter!

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: They said we'll be fine if we run somewhere where the sun is? Then let us hurry—benefactors?

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: ...Kroos.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Ready.

steps.name: Lava
steps.text: Good.

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: —Benefactors!? This is no time for jokes, we're no better than paste on our own! Let's hide before we do anything else!

steps.name: Mr. Nothing
steps.text: Here! Here, here! Why are you charging them! Alas! My good benefactors, you—wait for me, wait for me a moment!
